themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions in Central Harlem have deteriorated dramatically, with 43 complaints filed THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 4.8 per week—an 805% spike (z-score: 12.29)—suggesting a sudden infrastructure failure or neglect requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 43 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (805% increase)
Z-score of 12.29 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Combined with 231% spike in street/sidewalk noise complaints 2 weeks ago (153 vs. 46.2 avg), suggests systemic street degradation
reporting_angles: Visual canvass of major streets (125th St, Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Blvd, etc.) to document potholes, cracks, debris—photo essay potential
Interview DOT about whether there's a known maintenance backlog or weather-related emergency in CD110 this week

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 8 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.6 per week—a 1180% increase (z-score: 8.61)—marking the second-highest statistical anomaly and signaling either organized tagging activity or a delayed cleanup response.
evidence: 8 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (1180% spike, z-score: 8.61)
Represents sudden, sustained departure from near-zero baseline
Graffiti not listed in top 10 complaint categories overall (557 water leaks, 524 general complaints outpace it), suggesting concentrated outbreak
reporting_angles: Walk key corridors (125th St commercial strips, subway stations) to assess scope and tag style—identify if gang-related or artistic
Contact NYPD, Parks Dept. on cleanup timelines and whether they've detected organized crews in past 7 days

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 153 TWO WEEKS AGO (231% above the 46.2 weekly baseline, z-score: 6.54), and vehicle noise complaints peaked at 18 the same period (251% spike)—suggesting a specific event, construction project, or enforcement failure.
evidence: Street/sidewalk noise: 153 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 46.2 weekly average (231% spike, z-score: 6.54)
Vehicle noise: 18 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.1 weekly average (251% spike, z-score: 4.83)
Combined noise spike (street + vehicle + residential complaints totaling 3,973 over 90 days) is district's #2 complaint category
reporting_angles: Identify what construction or street work was underway 2 weeks ago—DOB permit filings show 23 new building projects and 376 alterations
Interview affected residents on specific noise sources and times; check if complaints cluster around particular blocks/hours

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Failures
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints jumped to 15 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 3.9 per week—a 287% spike (z-score: 5.33)—suggesting widespread outages or a failed maintenance cycle that may affect evening safety.
evidence: 15 street light complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.9 weekly average (287% spike, z-score: 5.33)
Aligns with broader street infrastructure crisis (805% spike in street condition complaints this week)
Street light failures directly impact public safety and quality of life in residential district
reporting_angles: Night-time photo survey of major intersections and residential blocks to identify dark zones
Contact Con Edison on whether there were outages or maintenance issues 2-3 weeks ago; check if complaints map to specific neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation complaints spiked to 5 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.2 per week—a 300% increase (z-score: 3.44)—possibly signaling confusion over new restrictions, billing issues, or pressure fluctuations affecting residents.
evidence: 5 water conservation complaints last week vs. 1.2 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 3.44)
Emerges amid district's ongoing heat/hot water crisis (8,230 complaints over 90 days, the dominant issue)
Low absolute volume but anomalous pattern warrants context check
reporting_angles: Verify if DEP issued new water-saving advisories or restrictions in the past 2 weeks that may have generated confusion
Cross-check against heat/hot water complaints to determine if residents are misreporting or if there's a real conservation messaging gap
